newsitem.title: USA: KAL Black boxes in "excellent condition".
newsitem.headline: KAL Black boxes in "excellent condition".

text.p: The black box flight recorders recovered from the Korean Air Lines crash site in Guam were in excellent shape and contained useful information, the National Transportation Safety Board said on Thursday.
"Both black boxes were received in excellent condition with virtually no damage to their exteriors. Both have usable data," the NTSB said in a statement.

Korean Air Flight 801 crashed on approach to Guam's international airport, with 254 people aboard. The plane's cockpit voice recorder and flight data recorder were quickly recovered and arrived at NTSB headquarters on Wednesday where they are being analysed.

The NTSB said experts began an initial analysis of the cockpit voice recorder on Wednesday night and began retrieving preliminary data from the flight recorder but that no information on their contents was available at this time.
The boxes, which are actually bright orange, were displayed at the NTSB offices.
They appeared to have suffered no fire damage and were barely even dented. Twenty-seven people survived the crash and 74 have been confirmed dead while 153 are still missing.
